explanation: The statement is about the library's own definitions: `ProjectiveClass`, `equivOfModuleEquivalence`, `classMap` and `finiteProjectiveEquivalence`. It says that equivalences whose functors are naturally isomorphic induce the same map on classes of finitely generated projective modules. Mathlib has no matching construction for these classes, so no Mathlib declaration can state this result. The proof uses only library lemmas (`classMap_of_reference`, `ProjectiveClass.of_eq_of_equiv`, `induction_on`) and generic tools (`AddEquiv.ext`, `Iso.toLinearEquiv`), which do not count. No separate search of the Mathlib sources was run, since the statement depends entirely on these library definitions.
